task.pr_title: [JAVA] Correct generation of schema default values of type object

cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description:
thanks for the pr.

i did a test with this test spec but got compilation errors

```
[INFO] Compiling 5 source files to C:\Users\wing3\AppData\Local\Temp\defaultvalue\target\test-classes
[INFO] -------------------------------------------------------------
[ERROR] COMPILATION ERROR :
[INFO] -------------------------------------------------------------
[ERROR] C:\Users\wing3\AppData\Local\Temp\defaultvalue\src\test\java\org\openapitools\client\model\TestTest.java:[34,31] error: Test is abstract; cannot be instantiated

```

is that expected?

evidence.thread_resolution:
DavidGrath: @wing328, no, it's not. Thank you, I'll try and look at it over the weekend
DavidGrath: @wing328, no, it's not. Thank you, I'll try and look at it over the weekend
DavidGrath: @wing328 , so I've seen the issue. JUnit's import took priority:
https://github.com/OpenAPITools/openapi-generator/blob/4379a23608f21bc622bd6e945915cf4aec41d426/modules/openapi-generator/src/main/resources/Java/model_test.mustache#L9
A simple fix would be to rename `Test`. I feel like it's also possible to fully qualify the `CodegenModel.classname`, but I don't think that functionality currently exists and it might not be worth it at all
wing328: one way to solve naming collision is to use the name mapping features to rename `Test` to something else

https://github.com/openapitools/openapi-generator/blob/master/docs/customization.md#name-mapping
